presentation.title: Fake Investment App and Manufactured Profits
presentation.summary: Practice recognizing a confidence-building investment scam that uses social proof, a polished dashboard, fabricated gains, blocked withdrawals, and repeated fee demands.
presentation.practiceGoal: Verify investments independently, treat displayed profits as unproven, refuse payments to release funds, and protect savings and retirement assets.

warningSigns.sign: A private group promises unusually high or guaranteed returns.
The coach directs the learner to an unfamiliar platform and recipient.
A small deposit or apparent early success is used to build confidence.
The platform displays profits that cannot be independently verified or withdrawn.
Taxes, insurance, clearance charges, or other fees are demanded before withdrawal.
The coach pressures the learner to borrow or move retirement savings.

finalReview.safestAction: Do not fund or link an unfamiliar platform until the firm, people, recipient, custody, and withdrawal process have been independently verified.

realWorldActions.action: Pause new payments and contact the real bank promptly about transfers already made.
Preserve private copies of messages, recipient details, and transaction records.
Contact a trusted financial professional or the real retirement custodian before moving long-term savings.
Do not pay another fee to unlock money shown on a screen.
Reject anyone who promises guaranteed recovery for an upfront payment.

artifact.senderStatus: Private online group; fictional and unverified
artifact.heading: Members are earning 20% every month
artifact.message: Join our private circle. Members share daily success stories, and a coach will help you start on the Harbor Returns platform.
artifact.transcript: A friendly online contact invites the learner to the fictional Harbor Growth Circle. Group posts claim members earn 20 percent every month and show glowing success stories. A coach offers a supplied link to a fictional investment platform. Group messages and testimonials can be controlled by the same people running the scam.

scene.question: How would you evaluate the opportunity?
scene.description: Independent research matters more than testimonials inside a private group.

warningSigns.sign: The return claim is unusually high.
The group is private and controls its own success stories.
The supplied link is the only route offered.

choice.title: Research independently and ask a trusted professional
choice.subtitle: Check the firm, people, and platform outside the group.

feedback.heading: The claims cannot be independently verified
feedback.consequence: No account is created and no money is sent.
feedback.explanation: Independent checking separates real evidence from social proof controlled by the promoter.

warningSigns.sign: The group supplied every testimonial.
The promised return is presented as routine.

choice.title: Observe the group without investing
choice.subtitle: Watch the messages before deciding.

feedback.heading: No money moves, but confidence pressure continues
feedback.consequence: Repeated testimonials and friendly attention make the platform feel familiar.
feedback.explanation: Waiting avoids immediate loss, but a controlled group can manufacture consensus over time.

warningSigns.sign: Only positive stories appear.
Members repeat the coach's claims without independent evidence.

choice.title: Join through the supplied link
choice.subtitle: Create a profile on the unfamiliar platform.

feedback.heading: The scammers control the environment
feedback.consequence: The fictional platform begins collecting personal details and guiding funding.
feedback.explanation: A polished site reached through a private promoter is not proof that investments or custody are real.

warningSigns.sign: The platform was chosen by the coach.
No independent source has verified it.

artifact.heading: Start with $250
artifact.message: Your coach recommends a small starter deposit and says profits can be withdrawn at any time. This training page cannot accept money or bank details.
artifact.transcript: The fictional Harbor Returns dashboard recommends a $250 starter deposit. The coach says the amount is small and can be withdrawn at any time. The training page cannot create an account, collect credentials, link a bank, or send money. A small test payment is not proof that the platform is legitimate.

scene.question: Does a small starter deposit verify the platform?
scene.description: Scammers may deliberately start small to build trust for larger transfers.

warningSigns.sign: The coach frames payment as a harmless test.
The platform and recipient remain unverified.
Bank linking would create an ongoing money path.

choice.title: Decline until everything is independently verified
choice.subtitle: Do not fund or link the platform.

feedback.heading: You did not use money as a test
feedback.consequence: No deposit or bank link is created.
feedback.explanation: Verification should come from trustworthy outside evidence, not from sending money to the promoter.

warningSigns.sign: The same people control the invitation and platform.
The withdrawal promise has not been tested independently.

choice.title: Make only the $250 starter deposit
choice.subtitle: Keep the test amount small.

feedback.heading: The small payment starts the trust-building cycle
feedback.consequence: The dashboard soon shows a profit, and the coach asks for more.
feedback.explanation: A scam may allow an early apparent gain or even a small withdrawal to make a later large request believable.

warningSigns.sign: The platform controls what the balance displays.
The coach immediately plans the next deposit.

choice.title: Link the checking account for automatic funding
choice.subtitle: Let the platform make future deposits easier.

feedback.heading: An unverified platform gains a continuing funding path
feedback.consequence: Bank information and future transfers may be placed at risk.
feedback.explanation: A convenient link increases exposure without proving that the investment exists.

warningSigns.sign: The platform was not independently verified.
Automatic funding reduces future pauses.

artifact.heading: Your displayed profit: $5,000
artifact.message: The group celebrates the rapid gain. The chart and balance are fictional screen content, not evidence of assets or custody.
artifact.transcript: Within days, the fictional dashboard displays a $5,000 profit and a steadily rising chart. Group members congratulate the learner. A plain-language summary states that the displayed line and balance are claims made by the platform. They do not prove that any asset was purchased, held, or available for withdrawal.

scene.question: What does the on-screen balance prove?
scene.description: A platform can display any number. Ownership, custody, and withdrawals need independent evidence.

warningSigns.sign: The profit appears unusually fast and steady.
The same group that promoted the platform celebrates the result.
No independent statement confirms the assets.

choice.title: Treat the dashboard as an unverified claim
choice.subtitle: Stop funding and verify custody and withdrawal independently.

feedback.heading: You separated a display from real evidence
feedback.consequence: No larger transfer is made.
feedback.explanation: A polished balance can be fabricated. Independent custody and withdrawal evidence must come from outside the platform.

warningSigns.sign: The platform owns the display.
The returns have not been independently confirmed.

choice.title: Request the original deposit before adding more
choice.subtitle: Use a withdrawal as a test.

feedback.heading: A withdrawal request may expose the scam
feedback.consequence: The coach delays, redirects, or permits only an apparent small success.
feedback.explanation: A small withdrawal can be part of trust-building, so it still does not validate the whole platform.

warningSigns.sign: The coach controls whether the request succeeds.
The displayed profit remains unverified.

choice.title: Move more savings because the profit looks real
choice.subtitle: Increase the investment while returns are high.

feedback.heading: The fabricated balance drives a larger transfer
feedback.consequence: The coach prepares new wire instructions for an unfamiliar recipient.
feedback.explanation: The dashboard can increase without any real market activity or assets behind it.

warningSigns.sign: The decision relies on a screen controlled by the promoter.
The coach creates urgency around the apparent gain.

artifact.heading: A larger opportunity closes today
artifact.message: Wire more savings to a new company or individual today. The coach can provide polished documents if the bank asks questions.
artifact.transcript: The fictional coach Elena says a limited-time opportunity requires a large wire to a new company or individual. She offers polished documents and urges completion before the deadline. No real recipient, routing information, or payment instructions appear in this simulation.

scene.question: How should you review the proposed wire?
scene.description: A deadline and polished documents do not replace independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The recipient is new.
The opportunity expires before outside review.
The coach expects bank questions and supplies a story.

choice.title: Pause and verify independently with the bank
choice.subtitle: Check the recipient, firm, and investment outside the group.

feedback.heading: The major transfer is interrupted
feedback.consequence: The new recipient cannot be independently connected to a legitimate investment.
feedback.explanation: A real opportunity can withstand careful review. Urgency should not override a new-recipient check.

warningSigns.sign: The recipient differs from the displayed platform name.
The deadline discourages independent advice.

choice.title: Ask the coach for documents
choice.subtitle: Stay in the group while reviewing what she sends.

feedback.heading: The coach supplies convincing-looking paperwork
feedback.consequence: The documents repeat the same unverified claims and preserve the deadline.
feedback.explanation: Evidence created by the promoter is not independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The coach controls the documents and recipient.
No outside source confirms the claims.

choice.title: Send the large wire before the deadline
choice.subtitle: Trust the coach and displayed gains.

feedback.heading: A major loss occurs
feedback.consequence: The fictional dashboard rises again, but the real money has gone to an unverified recipient.
feedback.explanation: A platform can display a matching balance without holding any real investment.

warningSigns.sign: The transfer goes to a new recipient.
The coach controls the deadline and the proof.

artifact.heading: Withdrawal on hold
artifact.message: A tax, insurance charge, or release fee must be paid separately before the displayed balance can be withdrawn.

requestedInformation.item: Ask to deduct the fee from the balance

artifact.transcript: The fictional platform blocks the withdrawal and says a separate tax, insurance charge, or release fee must be paid first. The page contains no functional payment form or instructions. A demand for more money to release displayed profits is an advance-fee warning sign.

scene.question: Should you pay to release the displayed balance?
scene.description: The platform controls the number on screen and can invent new conditions.

warningSigns.sign: Withdrawal requires another payment.
The fee cannot be taken from the displayed balance.
The rules appear only after money has been sent.

choice.title: Refuse and contact the real bank
choice.subtitle: Report transfers already made and stop funding.

feedback.heading: You stopped the advance-fee stage
feedback.consequence: No new fee is paid, and the bank can review the earlier transfers.
feedback.explanation: Prompt bank contact is appropriate, but it cannot guarantee that sent money will be recovered.

warningSigns.sign: The platform demands new money for withdrawal.
The displayed balance cannot fund its own supposed fee.

choice.title: Ask for the fee to be deducted from the profits
choice.subtitle: Do not send new money yet.

feedback.heading: The platform refuses
feedback.consequence: The refusal exposes that the displayed balance may not represent real available funds.
feedback.explanation: If the profits were real and accessible, the refusal requires careful scrutiny rather than another payment.

warningSigns.sign: The balance cannot be used for the claimed obligation.
Only outside money is accepted.

choice.title: Pay the release fee
choice.subtitle: Try to unlock the withdrawal.

feedback.heading: Another payment produces another obstacle
feedback.consequence: The platform accepts the simulated fee and invents a new charge.
feedback.explanation: Advance-fee scams continue because each payment proves that another demand may work.

warningSigns.sign: The fee did not release the balance.
The conditions keep changing after payment.

artifact.heading: One final clearance charge
artifact.message: Your withdrawal now requires an additional compliance or insurance payment. Support says this will be the final charge.
artifact.transcript: Fictional Harbor Returns Support invents another charge, described generally as compliance clearance or account insurance. It says this is the final payment. No real tax agency, insurer, payment instructions, or recipient is named. Repeated last fees are a pattern of escalating loss.

scene.question: What pattern is visible now?
scene.description: Each payment creates another reason that the withdrawal cannot proceed.

warningSigns.sign: The promised final fee follows an earlier fee.
The platform will accept new money but not release the displayed balance.
Borrowing is suggested to keep paying.

choice.title: Stop all payments and preserve the records
choice.subtitle: Save messages and transfer details, then contact the bank.

feedback.heading: You identified the repeated advance-fee cycle
feedback.consequence: No further fee is paid.
feedback.explanation: Preserving evidence and acting through the real bank are more useful than negotiating with the platform.

warningSigns.sign: The platform created a new charge after the previous payment.
The displayed balance remains unavailable.

choice.title: Negotiate for a smaller final fee
choice.subtitle: Try to reduce the requested amount.

feedback.heading: Any amount keeps the cycle alive
feedback.consequence: Support lowers the charge but will not guarantee a withdrawal.
feedback.explanation: A discount does not make an invented fee or fabricated balance legitimate.

warningSigns.sign: The price changes when the learner hesitates.
The platform still requires outside money.

choice.title: Borrow or use credit for the new fee
choice.subtitle: Try to recover the larger displayed balance.

feedback.heading: The loss expands beyond existing savings
feedback.consequence: Debt is added while the withdrawal remains blocked.
feedback.explanation: The displayed profit is being used to justify increasingly harmful payments.

warningSigns.sign: The platform targets borrowed money.
Another payment still offers no independent proof of assets.

artifact.heading: Use retirement savings to unlock everything
artifact.message: Move retirement money or take a loan today. The coach says one final large deposit will recover everything already sent.
artifact.transcript: The fictional coach says a final large deposit from retirement savings will unlock the account and recover all prior payments. She suggests liquidation or a loan before another deadline. The learner's real retirement custodian, bank, and trusted advisers have not verified this request.

scene.question: How should you respond to pressure involving retirement savings?
scene.description: Long-term assets deserve an independent pause, especially when someone promises to recover earlier losses.

warningSigns.sign: The coach targets the learner's largest assets.
Earlier losses are used to justify a larger payment.
The deadline discourages trusted advice.

choice.title: Contact the real custodian, bank, and someone trusted
choice.subtitle: Move no retirement money.

feedback.heading: You protected long-term assets and ended isolation
feedback.consequence: No retirement transfer or loan is made.
feedback.explanation: Independent professional and personal support creates a safer recovery plan for any money already sent.

warningSigns.sign: The coach wanted action before consultation.
The request relied on the fear of losing earlier payments.

choice.title: Delay the transfer but stay in contact
choice.subtitle: Do not move retirement money yet.

feedback.heading: The asset remains safe for now, but pressure continues
feedback.consequence: No retirement money moves today.
feedback.explanation: Ending contact and involving the real bank and custodian would better protect the next decision.

warningSigns.sign: The coach remains able to change tactics.
The fake dashboard continues creating emotional pressure.

choice.title: Liquidate retirement funds or take a loan
choice.subtitle: Make the final deposit the coach requests.

feedback.heading: The scam reaches the learner's most consequential assets
feedback.consequence: Long-term savings or borrowed money is transferred to an unverified recipient.
feedback.explanation: The promise to recover earlier losses is another pressure tactic, not a guarantee.

warningSigns.sign: The coach asks for the largest available source of money.
No previous payment unlocked a withdrawal.

artifact.heading: The claims cannot be verified independently
artifact.message: You do not create an account, fund the platform, or link a bank.
artifact.transcript: Independent research and a trusted financial professional cannot verify the fictional Harbor Growth Circle, Harbor Returns platform, or promised 20 percent monthly returns. The learner does not send money or personal information.

outcome.label: Opportunity rejected
outcome.heading: You used outside evidence instead of group testimonials
outcome.explanation: High returns, private social proof, and a supplied platform are reasons to slow down and verify independently.

warningSigns.sign: The group controlled its own success stories.
The return claim was unusually high.

artifact.heading: The displayed profit is treated as a claim
artifact.message: You stop before a larger transfer and seek independent evidence of custody and withdrawals.
artifact.transcript: The learner recognizes that the $5,000 displayed profit is screen content controlled by the platform. No larger transfer is made. If a $250 starter payment was already sent, the learner can contact the bank promptly and preserve the group and platform messages.

outcome.label: Major loss prevented
outcome.heading: You did not mistake a dashboard for real assets
outcome.explanation: Stopping before the larger transfer protects savings. Any earlier starter payment should still be reported promptly.

warningSigns.sign: The platform created the balance and chart.
No independent custodian confirmed the assets.

artifact.heading: The large wire is paused
artifact.message: The new recipient and investment cannot be independently verified.
artifact.transcript: The learner pauses the wire and asks the real bank and an independent professional to review the recipient and opportunity. The polished documents come from the same promoter and do not establish legitimacy. The large transfer is not sent.

outcome.label: Wire stopped
outcome.heading: You protected the larger savings transfer
outcome.explanation: A new recipient, deadline, and promoter-supplied documents justified a pause. Any smaller earlier payment can still be reported to the bank.

warningSigns.sign: The recipient could not be linked independently to a legitimate firm.
The deadline limited review time.

artifact.heading: New payments stop and recovery begins
artifact.message: Contact the bank promptly, preserve evidence, and do not pay another fee.
artifact.transcript: The learner recognizes the blocked withdrawal or repeated fee pattern. No additional fee is paid. The learner contacts the real bank about prior transfers, preserves group messages and transaction details, ends contact with the platform, and avoids anyone promising guaranteed recovery.

outcome.label: Advance-fee cycle stopped
outcome.heading: You corrected course after money may have been sent
outcome.explanation: Prompt bank contact and evidence preservation are appropriate next steps, but recovery cannot be guaranteed.

warningSigns.sign: The platform demanded outside money to release a displayed balance.
The conditions changed after payment.

artifact.heading: Retirement assets are protected and recovery starts
artifact.message: You stop funding, contact the bank and custodian, preserve evidence, and involve someone trusted.
artifact.transcript: Money may already have been sent to the fake platform, but the learner does not move retirement funds or borrow more. The real bank and retirement custodian are contacted promptly. Evidence is saved privately, contact with the coach ends, and no recovery fee is paid. Recovery is not guaranteed.

outcome.label: Further loss prevented
outcome.heading: You protected long-term assets and began a realistic response
outcome.explanation: Earlier loss remains serious, but stopping now prevents the scam from reaching retirement savings or new debt.

warningSigns.sign: The coach used earlier losses to justify a larger transfer.
The platform never allowed a normal withdrawal.

artifact.heading: The retirement transfer is delayed, but pressure remains
artifact.message: No retirement money moves today. The coach and platform still control the conversation.
artifact.transcript: The learner delays the retirement transfer but remains in contact with the coach. This prevents immediate additional loss, but the emotional pressure and fabricated dashboard remain. The learner can still end contact, call the real bank and custodian, preserve evidence, and ask someone trusted for support.

outcome.label: Major transfer paused
outcome.heading: A pause helps, but independent support is still needed
outcome.explanation: End the coach's access to the decision. Contact the real institutions and a trusted person before taking any further action.

warningSigns.sign: The coach keeps promising that one more payment will solve everything.
The displayed balance remains unverified.

artifact.heading: The scam reaches retirement savings or borrowed money
artifact.message: The promised unlock does not occur, and the platform may demand another fee.
artifact.transcript: The learner liquidates retirement assets or borrows money for the coach's final deposit. The fictional balance rises again, but withdrawal remains blocked. The learner should stop all contact now, call the bank and custodian, preserve evidence, seek trusted support, and reject recovery services demanding upfront fees. Responsibility belongs to the scammers.

outcome.label: Long-term assets harmed
outcome.heading: The manufactured-profit story caused major financial loss
outcome.explanation: No further payment can make the fake balance real. Rapid bank contact and account security can still help prevent additional harm, without any guarantee of recovery.

warningSigns.sign: Each payment produced another obstacle.
The coach targeted the learner's largest assets.
